blurb:
Marietta Melt Yard on Whitlock is a solid pick when you want to meet up with family for lunch and nobody wants to argue about where to go. We ended up here with a mixed group and it worked for everyone, which is harder to pull off than it sounds. Good for casual weekday lunches, weekend get-togethers, or whenever you want something filling without overthinking it.

The food is on the heavier, greasier side, which some people love and some don't. If that's your thing, you'll be happy. If you're watching it, just know going in. The service gets consistent praise, and they're open seven days a week through the dinner hour.

One small thing worth knowing: some reviewers noted the food ran a little greasy, but the same people said they'd come back and try something different next time. That tells you something about the place.

blurb:
The Wing Cafe on Roswell Road is the spot you go when the game is on, the weather is good, and you want a cold beer with something worth eating. High energy, loud in the best way, and they've got an outdoor tiki bar with live music on top of it all. Great for game day, post-work hangouts, or any Friday night where you want to feel like you're actually doing something.

Wings are obviously the reason you show up. They know what they're doing. Pair that with a craft beer from the tap selection and you're in good shape. This is pub food done well, not an afterthought.

They're open every single day until 11pm, so there's almost no bad time to go.

blurb:
Laredos on Sandy Plains is exactly what you want from a neighborhood Mexican spot. Colorful room, traditional decorations, friendly vibe. Good for a weeknight dinner when you don't want to cook, or a Friday night out with a couple of friends where you're not looking to spend a fortune.

The Mexican classics are what people come for, and the margaritas are a big part of why they keep coming back. If you haven't been, start there and work your way through the menu.

They stay open until 10pm most nights and 10:30pm on Fridays and Saturdays, so there's no rush if you're heading over after a long day.

blurb:
This place is a legit hidden gem on Allgood Road and I don't say that lightly. It's a supermarket with a taqueria tucked inside, and the food coming out of that kitchen is the real deal. People walk past it all the time without knowing what's in there. Good for a cheap, no-frills lunch or a quick dinner when you want something homemade and filling.

The al pastor is what you need to order. Reviewers are very specific about it: well seasoned, cooked right, not overdone. The pupusas are also getting a lot of love, especially the beans and cheese. And the chicken plate with rice and beans is worth knowing about too. The beans are made from scratch, not from a can, and you can taste the difference.

Thursdays they close earlier than the rest of the week, around 6:50pm, so plan around that if Thursday is your day.

blurb:
This is one of those spots I tell people about and they always come back saying they can't believe it took them this long to go. Brazilian Bakery Cafe on Powers Ferry is a cheery, casual place that does Brazilian light bites and an impressive spread of traditional cakes and cookies. Good for a slow weekend morning, a midday coffee break, or honestly just stopping in after running errands because the smell will get you every time.

The traditional cakes and cookies are the reason people keep coming back. If you haven't tried Brazilian baked goods before, this is a great introduction. The portions are solid and the prices are easy on the wallet.

They're open pretty much every day starting at 6:30am, with Sunday starting at 8. So whether it's a weekday morning or a lazy Sunday, they've got you covered.
